subject.title: [Feature]: Invoke tools directly without LLM round-trip

question: Which remaining direct-invoke surfaces beyond shipped HTTP/RPC/SDK, skill-command dispatch, and command cron should OpenClaw core support, and what owner/security gates are required?
rationale: The unresolved scope can expose filesystem, process, session, cron, Gateway, and node actions without a model turn, so automation cannot safely choose the product boundary or trust model.

options.title: Keep the umbrella and review narrow gated slices
options.body: Leave this issue open while reviewing the active host-FS and readiness PRs with explicit owner gates, safe defaults, audit coverage, docs, and live proof before merge.

options.title: Declare shipped paths sufficient
options.body: Close this umbrella after maintainers decide that HTTP/RPC/SDK, skill-command dispatch, and command cron are the only supported direct-invoke surfaces for now.

options.title: Approve broader direct execution
options.body: Support broader direct execution only with a named security design, operator controls, compatibility proof, and user-facing documentation before implementation.

recommendation.title: Keep the umbrella and review narrow gated slices
recommendation.body: Leave this issue open while reviewing the active host-FS and readiness PRs with explicit owner gates, safe defaults, audit coverage, docs, and live proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice is primarily the dangerous-tool and Gateway operator boundary, and history ties Peter Steinberger to that code and policy area.
